chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Hajj is in known months: Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and Dhu al-Hijja. So whoever intends to perform Hajj should let his hair grow when he sees the crescent of Dhu al-Qadah, and whoever intends to perform Umrah should let his hair grow for a month.
ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim start letting their hair grow before Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific temporal markers for entering the state of Ihram, linking the ritual preparation to the sighting of the Dhu al-Qadah crescent for Hajj and a fixed month for Umrah. It reflects the scholarly understanding of the 'known months' (ashhur ma'lumat) mentioned in the Quran, emphasizing the physical manifestation of spiritual readiness through letting hair grow before donning the Ihram garments.
